name: Marketing, web or design agency
description: An agency or studio: services, case studies, the team, clients' questions and job openings, with facts about the focus, team size, where and in which languages you work, the usual budget and awards.

questions.question: What does the agency specialise in – which kind of work and which clients?
questions.help: One sentence a client would recognise, e.g. "websites and online shops for manufacturers".

questions.question: In which year was the agency founded?
How many people work at the agency?
questions.help: Count the people clients actually work with; mention regular freelancers elsewhere rather than in this number.

questions.question: Where are your clients – a city, a country, internationally?
In which languages can clients work with you?
From what budget do you usually take on a project?
questions.help: An amount with the currency. It saves both sides a call; leave it empty if you prefer not to say.

questions.question: Has the agency or its work won any awards? Which ones and when?
questions.help: Only awards actually won, with the year. Leave it empty if there are none.

audit.message: Add at least three case studies – clients choose an agency by its work. Publish only projects the client has agreed to.
Add the services you offer, each with what the client gets and how you work.
Introduce the team – clients want to know who they will work with.
Say in one sentence what the agency specialises in.
Publish a privacy policy page – the contact form and job applications collect personal data; check what your law requires.

claude: An agency's site is its own showcase: clients judge it by the work it shows, so the case studies lead and each one tells the brief, what the agency did and the result – stated as the client confirms it. Describe services as what the client gets and how the collaboration runs, in plain words rather than buzzwords. Never invent clients, logos, projects, results or percentages, quotes, awards, partner badges or team members – ask the owner for each, publish a client's name or logo only with consent, and describe work under NDA without naming the client only if the owner agrees. Team members appear with their own consent and a real photo. Every job opening needs a closing date so it hides itself. Keep the focus, team size and the usual budget as facts so the site states them the same everywhere.
